summary: IDS s166_triple has degraded visibility: 63% of TCP sessions are one-way (needs both directions), microbursts to 2.06 Gbps overload the 1 Gbps tool port (206% capacity), and 66.9% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% tolerance for payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction of bidirectional flows. 104 of 165 TCP sessions (63.0%) are unidirectional, well above 10% threshold. Most likely SPAN/mirror configured for TX or RX only, or only one leg of an asymmetric routed path is tapped without bidirectional aggregation at the broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions for TCP reassembly, state tracking and signature matching. With only one side, it misses handshakes, cannot track sessions, and fails to detect attacks that span request/response, causing major detection gaps and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions (e.g., TAP A + TAP B or TX+RX) into a single coherent feed at the packet broker so the IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions for accurate stateful detection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic bursts peak at 2.06 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (206% overload, 2 overloaded intervals). Broker is forwarding full aggregated traffic out a single 1G tool port with no load-balancing, policing or burst buffering.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts. Even without broker drops yet, the tool itself will drop, causing missed signatures, incomplete flows, and blind spots exactly during high-volume events when detection is most critical.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple 1G IDS ports/instances with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port rate under 80% and absorb microbursts, preventing tool-side drops while preserving flow coherence.

findings.root_cause: 66.9% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is sent to the IDS still encrypted with no upstream decryption or selective bypass, so payload is opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for deep packet inspection and signatures. With two-thirds encrypted, it can only do metadata/heuristics, sharply reducing detection coverage for payload-based exploits, malware and C2 inside TLS.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS centrally before the IDS (or feed decrypted copy) and bypass undecryptable privacy traffic, bringing encrypted share below 60% so IDS can inspect cleartext payloads it was designed to analyze.
